title: Fills with the Tom
description: Learn the sounds that make up a drum fill, the short burst that carries a song into its next section.

steps.title: What's a fill?
steps.description: A fill is when the drummer stops playing the groove for a moment and does something different, usually across the snare and toms. It might last one beat or a whole bar. It works like a heads-up to the listener and the band: something new is about to start. Most fills end with a crash on the next beat 1, right as the new section lands. In a real fill these hits come one after another. Here we'll practise them as pairs so you get to know the sounds.

steps.title: The tom on its own
steps.description: Hit the tom. It's deeper and rounder than the snare, and it has more of a note to it. That's why fills sound like they're moving somewhere.
steps.hint: Bottom row, second from the left, labelled TOM.

steps.title: Snare and tom
steps.description: A lot of fills start on the snare and move down to the toms. Hit the snare and tom together to hear how the two sounds sit next to each other.
steps.hint: SNR is on the top row, and TOM is right below it.

steps.title: Tom and kick
steps.description: Now hit the tom and kick together. Fills often work their way down in pitch, and a kick under the last tom hit makes the bottom of the fill hit harder.
steps.hint: KCK is top left, and TOM is one row down and one pad to the right.

steps.title: Tom into crash
steps.description: Hit the tom and crash together. Think of it as the last note of the fill running straight into the crash that starts the next section.
steps.hint: They're next to each other on the bottom row: TOM, then CRS.

steps.title: Land it
steps.description: Finish with the kick and crash together. That's the landing, beat 1 of the new section, where the fill ends and the groove comes back in.
steps.hint: KCK top left, CRS on the bottom row. Make it feel like a full stop.
